newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ approves open skies agreement with U.S.
newsitem.headline: NZ approves open skies agreement with U.S.

text.p: New Zealand's cabinet has approved an air transport agreement, or "open skies" deal, struck with the United States late last month and it should be signed next week, the New Zealand Press Association said on Monday.
The agreement was negotiated 10 days ago by New Zealand and U.S. officials. Transport Minister Jenny Shipley said she had been authorised to sign it while on a scheduled trip next week.

The agreement permits unrestricted airline activity between the two countries. Shipley said it had the potential to increase tourism to New Zealand and airlines may take up the opportunity to fly to more cities in the U.S. beyond the west coast gateways.

"The removal of all restrictions on international air services operated by New Zealand airlines to, from and beyond the United States will assist in maximising the profile of New Zealand in that market," she said.

"It's also an important agreement for exporters and importers as it means that the airlines of one country may establish cargo services which operate solely between the other country and third countries.
